senses.title: To have a sense
senses.definition: to have as a meaning, said of a word, sign or gesture
senses.definitionCN: 指词语、符号或手势所具有的意思
senses.example: What does this symbol mean?
senses.exampleCN: 这个符号表示什么？
senses.why: The Old English verb mænan meant 'to intend, signify', and a word's sense is what it intends.
senses.whyCN: 古英语动词 mænan 意为「意图、意指」，而词的意思就是它所意图的东西。

senses.title: To be a sign of
senses.definition: to be a sign or indication of something else
senses.definitionCN: 作为另一件事的迹象或征兆
senses.example: A red sky at night means fair weather tomorrow.
senses.exampleCN: 傍晚的红霞意味着明天天气晴好。
senses.why: A sign points to what it intends, so the verb extends from words to natural signs.
senses.whyCN: 符号指向它所意指之物，于是这个动词从词语扩展到自然征兆。

senses.title: To intend to do
senses.definition: to have something in mind as a purpose
senses.definitionCN: 把某事放在心里作为目的
senses.example: I mean to finish the report tonight.
senses.exampleCN: 我打算今晚把报告写完。
senses.why: Intention is the inward side of meaning: what a person means is what he intends.
senses.whyCN: 意图是「意思」的内面：一个人意指什么，就是他打算什么。

senses.title: The average of a set
senses.definition: the value obtained by adding all the numbers and dividing by how many there are
senses.definitionCN: 把全部数值相加再除以个数所得的值
senses.example: Add the values and divide by five to get the mean.
senses.exampleCN: 把这些值相加再除以五，就得到平均值。
senses.why: This sense comes from a different source: Old French meien 'middle', from Latin medianus, not from the English verb.
senses.whyCN: 这一义出自另一来源：古法语 meien「中间」，上溯拉丁 medianus，与英语动词无关。

senses.title: The middle between extremes
senses.definition: a middle point equally distant from two extremes
senses.definitionCN: 与两个极端等距的中间点
senses.example: The golden mean lies between excess and defect.
senses.exampleCN: 中庸之道位于过度与不足之间。
senses.why: The same 'middle' sense serves ethics as well as arithmetic, naming the point that is neither too much nor too little.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「中间」义既用于算术也用于伦理，指既不过多也不过少的那一点。

senses.title: Unkind in manner
senses.definition: unkind, spiteful or deliberately hurtful
senses.definitionCN: 不友善、带恶意或故意伤人的
senses.example: It was mean of him to laugh at her mistake.
senses.exampleCN: 他嘲笑她的错误，未免刻薄。
senses.why: The adjective comes from a third source, Old English gemæne 'common, shared', whose sense sank from 'common' to 'inferior' and then to 'petty'.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词出自第三个来源，古英语 gemæne「共同的、共享的」，词义从「共同」降到「低劣」，再降到「小气」。

senses.title: Stingy with money
senses.definition: unwilling to spend or share what one has
senses.definitionCN: 不愿花钱或不愿分享所有
senses.example: He is too mean to buy a second chair.
senses.exampleCN: 他太吝啬，连第二把椅子都不肯买。
senses.why: A person who keeps everything for himself is 'common' in the old sense of ordinary and small, and the word settled into stinginess.
senses.whyCN: 把一切都留给自己的人在旧义上显得「普通而小气」，于是这个词固定为吝啬。

senses.title: Remarkable in the phrase 'no mean'
senses.titleCN: 固定说法中意为「不小的」
senses.definition: not small or easy, used in the fixed phrase no mean feat
senses.definitionCN: 不小、不容易，用于固定说法「不小的成就」
senses.example: Finishing the climb in one day was no mean feat.
senses.exampleCN: 一天之内爬完这段路可不是小事。
senses.why: The phrase works by understatement: it denies the small reading of the adjective in order to praise.
senses.whyCN: 这个说法用反语：否定形容词「小」的那一面，从而达到称赞。

intro.en: Mean has three separate sources that happen to share one spelling: the verb 'to intend' from Old English mænan, the noun 'average' from Old French meien and Latin medianus, and the adjective 'petty, stingy' from Old English gemæne 'common'.
intro.cn: mean 有三个恰好同形的来源：表示「意图」的动词出自古英语 mænan；表示「平均值」的名词出自古法语 meien 与拉丁 medianus；表示「小气、刻薄」的形容词出自古英语 gemæne「共同的」。

items.en: Mænan meant 'to intend, signify'. Its deeper Germanic origin is not settled; the usual comparison with German meinen is a family resemblance rather than a proved derivation.
items.cn: mænan 意为「意图、意指」。其更早的日耳曼来源无定论；通常把它与德语 meinen 相比，那只是同族相似，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: Gemæne meant 'common, shared'. The sense passed from 'common' to 'ordinary, inferior' and then to 'petty, stingy', a downward slide recorded in Middle English.
items.cn: gemæne 意为「共同的、共享的」。词义从「共同」经「普通、低劣」滑向「小气、吝啬」，这一下移在中古英语中已有记录。

items.en: Meien 'middle' entered English in the fourteenth century as the name of the middle value, and it is the source of the average sense.
items.cn: meien「中间」在十四世纪进入英语，指居中的那个数值，是平均值义的来源。

items.en: Medianus 'of the middle' comes from medius 'middle', the same root that gives median, medium and mediate.
items.cn: medianus「中间的」出自 medius「中间」，同一词根还给出 median、medium、mediate。

items.en: English spelling merged the three histories into one written form, which is why a single entry must keep verb, average and adjective apart.
items.cn: 英语拼写把这三段历史并成一个书写形式，因此同一个词条必须把动词、平均值与形容词分开。

items.en: Exact first citations for each strand are approximate: the verb is Old English, the average noun is fourteenth-century, and the stingy adjective is later Middle English.
items.cn: 三条线索的确切首见书证都只是约数：动词属古英语，平均值名词属十四世纪，吝啬形容词属中古英语后期。

note.en: Group one holds forms and relatives that are easily mistaken for the same word; group two holds words that share one of the three meanings.
note.cn: 第一组是容易被当成同一个词的形式与亲属词；第二组是分别与三种含义之一相近的词。

entries.definition: The third-person singular of the verb, and separately a plural noun meaning 'resources'; it is not the adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 动词的第三人称单数，另有一个表示「资源、手段」的复数名词；都不是那个形容词。

entries.definition: The past tense and participle of the verb; the spelling no longer shows the vowel of the base.
entries.definitionCN: 动词的过去式与过去分词；拼写已看不出原形元音。

entries.definition: From the same Latin root as the average sense, but it names the middle item of an ordered set, not the sum divided by the count.
entries.definitionCN: 与平均值义同出拉丁词根，但指按序排列后居中的那一项，而非总和除以个数。

entries.definition: Latin medius as a noun: the middle, or a means between two sides; it has nothing to do with intending.
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁 medius 的名词形式：中间，或两端之间的媒介；与「意图」无关。

entries.definition: The everyday word for the sum divided by the count; mean is its technical doublet in statistics.
entries.definitionCN: 日常说法，指总和除以个数；在统计中 mean 是它的技术性同义词。

entries.definition: To be a sign of something, close to the 'be a sign' sense of mean.
entries.definitionCN: 作为某事的符号，接近 mean 的「预示」义。

entries.definition: To have a purpose, the plain equivalent of the 'plan' sense.
entries.definitionCN: 怀有目的，是「打算」义的直白对应词。

entries.definition: Unwilling to spend or share, the direct synonym of the adjective in its money sense.
entries.definitionCN: 不愿花钱或分享，是形容词在钱财义上的直接同义词。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定说法与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Three histories share one spelling: intend, middle, and common-turned-petty.
normal.cn: 三段历史共用一种拼写：意图、中间、由「共同」转来的小气。

normal.en: The verb is irregular in sound but regular in pattern: means, meant, meant, meaning.
normal.cn: 动词读音不规则但形式规律：三单、过去式、过去分词、现在分词依次为 means、meant、meant、meaning。

normal.en: Fixed phrases sort the senses: mean to do, mean well, the mean value, no mean feat.
normal.cn: 固定说法把义项分开：打算做、出于好意、平均值、不小的成就。

normal.en: The average sense came through French, so it belongs with median and medium rather than with the verb.
normal.cn: 平均值义经法语而来，因此它与 median、medium 同族，而不属于动词那一支。

normal.en: The unkind sense began as 'common', which then meant 'ordinary' and finally 'petty'.
normal.cn: 刻薄义起于「共同的」，再变成「普通的」，最后成了「小气的」。

abstract.en: Picture a hand pointing at the one thing a vague sentence was trying to say.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手指出一句含混的话真正想说的那件事。

abstract.en: Picture a pair of scales settling exactly level, with equal weights on both sides.
abstract.cn: 想象一架天平恰好停在水平位置，两边重量相等。

abstract.en: Picture a man counting coins twice before he will spend a single one.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人把硬币数了两遍才肯花掉一枚。

examples.en: A green light means that the road is clear.
examples.cn: 绿灯表示道路畅通。

examples.en: The mean of the class scores rose after the extra lesson.
examples.cn: 加课之后，全班成绩的平均值上升了。

examples.en: It was mean of them to leave her out of the invitation.
examples.cn: 他们把她排除在邀请之外，实在刻薄。

dict_mnemonic.text: 动词那一支表示「意图、意指」；平均值那一支来自法语里的「中间」；形容词那一支从「共同的」滑到「普通」，再滑到「小气」。三支同形，要按上下文分开。

root: 三条互不同源的线索合成一个拼写：动词出自古英语 mænan「意图、意指」，更早来源无定论；平均值义出自古法语 meien「中间」，上溯拉丁 medianus、medius；形容词义出自古英语 gemæne「共同的」，词义下滑为「低劣、小气」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses come from three histories: intending and signifying, the middle value, and the small or petty. The entry keeps them apart so that no sentence is read through the wrong history.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项来自三段历史：意图与意指、居中的数值、以及小气刻薄。本词条把它们分开，免得用错历史去读一个句子。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand points at what a sentence intends, while a balance beside it rests exactly level.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手指出一句话所意图的东西，旁边的天平恰好水平。

branches.en: SIGNIFY: a word and a red sky both point to what they intend.
branches.cn: 意指：一个词与一片红霞都指向它们所意图的东西。

branches.en: INTEND: purpose is what a person means to do.
branches.cn: 意图：目的就是一个人打算做的事。

branches.en: THE MIDDLE: the average and the golden mean are one position seen numerically and ethically.
branches.cn: 中间：平均值与中庸是同一点在数字与伦理上的两个看法。

branches.en: COMMON TO PETTY: the adjective slid from shared to ordinary to stingy.
branches.cn: 由共同到小气：形容词从「共享」滑到「普通」再到「吝啬」。

branches.en: UNDERSTATEMENT: denying 'small' is a way of saying 'large'.
branches.cn: 反语：否定「小」，正是说「大」。

intro.en: One spelling serves three families, so the affix view must be split: a Germanic verb, a Germanic adjective, and a Latin root for the middle.
intro.cn: 一种拼写服务于三个词族，因此按语素读时必须拆开：一个日耳曼动词、一个日耳曼形容词，以及一个表示「中间」的拉丁词根。

latinIntro.en: The verb family is Germanic, with no Latin kin; the average sense belongs to Latin medius, which also gives median, medium and mediate.
latinIntro.cn: 动词一族属日耳曼语，没有拉丁同族；平均值义属拉丁 medius，同根还给出 median、medium、mediate。

items.exampleCN: 这个形容词从「共享」开始，最后落到「吝啬」。

definition_zh: 与此同时；在此期间；其间；那段时间
definition_en: during the time between two events, or at the same time as something else is happening
core_image: 两条并排的时间线都在往前走，中间连着一条细线
scene: 客厅里电视还开着，厨房的水壶已经开始响。She kept stirring the soup; meanwhile the guests arrived one by one.
sceneCN: 这里是「与此同时」（第 2 个义项：两件事并行发生）；句意为她一直搅着汤，与此同时客人陆续到了。

collocations.zh: 与此同时，在别处（戏谑转场语）

derivatives.zh: 由 mean（居间的）与 time 复合而成，与 meanwhile 并行使用，义为「其间；同时」
meanwhile 的前半部分，作形容词时义为「中间的；居中的」
meanwhile 的后半部分，作名词时义为「一段时间」

senses.title: During the interval between two events
senses.titleCN: 在此期间；两件事之间的空当
senses.definition: in the period of time between one event and another
senses.definitionCN: 在一件事与另一件事之间的那段时间里
senses.example: The first film ended at nine; meanwhile the second hall was still filling up.
senses.exampleCN: 第一场电影九点散场，在此期间第二个放映厅还在进人。
senses.why: Meanwhile was built from mean, meaning middle or intervening, and while, meaning a stretch of time, so its first job was to name the gap between two moments.
senses.whyCN: meanwhile 由 mean（中间的、居间的）与 while（一段时间）构成，所以它最初的任务就是命名两个时刻之间的空当。

senses.title: At the same time, as a contrast
senses.definition: at the same time as something else, especially when the two developments are being contrasted
senses.definitionCN: 与另一件事同时发生，尤用于对比两种变化
senses.example: Prices kept rising; meanwhile wages stayed flat.
senses.exampleCN: 物价持续上涨，与此同时工资原地不动。
senses.why: Because the gap between two events is also a span shared by them, the word came to mark two lines of action running side by side.
senses.whyCN: 既然两件事之间的空当也是二者共有的时段，这个词就转而标记两条并排推进的行动线。

senses.title: The time between two events as a noun
senses.definition: the period of time between two events, used with the as a noun
senses.definitionCN: 两件事之间的那段时间，加 the 作名词使用
senses.example: In the meanwhile, the children played in the yard.
senses.exampleCN: 在这段时间里，孩子们在院子里玩。
senses.why: English often turns an adverb of time into a noun by adding the, and the meanwhile names the stretch itself rather than the relation between events.
senses.whyCN: 英语常用加 the 的办法把时间副词变成名词，the meanwhile 指的就是那段时间本身，而不是事件之间的关系。

intro.en: Meanwhile is a compound of two older words: mean in its middle sense and while in its time sense.
intro.cn: meanwhile 是两个更古老的词复合而成：取「中间」义的 mean 与取「时间」义的 while。

items.en: Latin medianus meant middle or central, and it reached English through French as the adjective mean.
items.cn: 拉丁语 medianus 意为中间的、中央的，经法语进入英语，成为形容词 mean。

items.en: Old French meien kept the middle sense and supplied the form that English shortened to mean.
items.cn: 古法语 meien 保留了「中间」的意思，提供了英语缩略为 mean 的词形。

items.en: Old English hwīl meant a period of time, and it is the word behind while.
items.cn: 古英语 hwīl 意为一段时间，是 while 的来源。

items.en: Middle English used the phrase in the mean while, literally in the intervening time.
items.cn: 中古英语使用 in the mean while 这一短语，字面意思是「在居间的那段时间里」。

items.en: The phrase was compressed into the single adverb meanwhile, and a noun use with the followed.
items.cn: 这个短语被压缩成单个副词 meanwhile，随后又出现了加 the 的名词用法。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the compound's two halves and its twin; the near-meaning group collects adverbs of simultaneous timing.
note.cn: 形近组收这个复合词的两半和它的孪生词；近义组收表示同时发生的副词。

entries.definition: A parallel compound meaning the intervening time.
entries.definitionCN: 并行的复合词，意为其间的那段时间。

entries.definition: As an adjective, middle or average.
entries.definitionCN: 作形容词时意为中间的、平均的。

entries.definition: A period of time, or during the time that.
entries.definitionCN: 一段时间，或「在……期间」。

entries.definition: A chiefly British variant of while.
entries.definitionCN: while 的英式变体。

entries.definition: At exactly the same time.
entries.definitionCN: 在同一时刻。

entries.definition: At the same time, often of events running in parallel.
entries.definitionCN: 同时发生，常指并行的事件。

entries.definition: Both at the same time, in one phrase.
entries.definitionCN: 短语，表示同时。

normalIntro.en: The word is a phrase welded into one adverb, built from a middle word and a time word.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是一个被焊成副词短语的组合，由「中间」的词与「时间」的词搭成。

normal.en: Mean here is not the verb meaning intend; it is the old adjective for middle.
normal.cn: 这里的 mean 不是表示「打算」的动词，而是古老的形容词「中间的」。

normal.en: While is the time word, so meanwhile literally means in the middle of the time.
normal.cn: while 是时间词，所以 meanwhile 字面上就是「在时间中间」。

normal.en: Meantime is built on time instead of while, which is why the two words are so close in meaning.
normal.cn: meantime 用 time 而不是 while 来构成，所以两个词的意思非常接近。

normal.en: The phrase in the meanwhile shows the noun use, with the standing before the compound.
normal.cn: in the meanwhile 展示了名词用法，the 就放在这个复合词前面。

normal.en: The two halves still live separately: mean as middle and while as a stretch of time.
normal.cn: 两半仍然各自独立：mean 表示中间，while 表示一段时间。

abstract.en: Two clocks side by side keep their own pace, and the space between them is the meanwhile.
abstract.cn: 两只并排的钟各走各的，二者之间的空隙就是 meanwhile。

abstract.en: Think of a film cutting between two rooms, the camera saying meanwhile without a word.
abstract.cn: 想一部电影在两个房间之间切换，镜头不说话就完成了「与此同时」。

abstract.en: English often welds a phrase into one word, and meanwhile is a whole clause shrunk to a signal.
abstract.cn: 英语常把短语焊成一个词，meanwhile 就是一整句关系被压缩成一个信号。

examples.en: She kept stirring the soup; meanwhile the guests arrived one by one.
examples.cn: 她一直搅着汤，与此同时客人陆续到了。

examples.en: Prices kept rising; meanwhile wages stayed flat.
examples.cn: 物价持续上涨，与此同时工资原地不动。

examples.en: In the meanwhile, the children played in the yard.
examples.cn: 在这段时间里，孩子们在院子里玩。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「民外」——屋里忙着，民外也在忙；记住 meanwhile 是与此同时。

root: 由 mean（中间的，源自拉丁语 medianus，经古法语 meien 入英语）与 while（一段时间，古英语 hwīl）复合，字面义为「在居间的那段时间里」。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the span shared by two happenings; the senses divide into the interval, the parallel contrast, and the interval treated as a noun.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是两件事共有的那段时间；义项分成居间的空当、并行的对比，以及被当作名词的那段时间。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two time lines running forward side by side, joined by a thin line between them.
core.cn: 核心意象：两条并排向前的时间线，中间连着一条细线。

branches.en: two events with a gap between them
branches.cn: 两件事之间留出一段空当

branches.en: two lines of action running at once
branches.cn: 两条行动线同时推进

branches.en: a noun phrase with the in front
branches.cn: 前面加 the 的名词短语

branches.en: a film cutting from one room to another
branches.cn: 电影从一个房间切到另一个房间

branches.en: two graphs rising in opposite directions
branches.cn: 两条曲线朝相反方向走

intro.en: The word is supported by a Latin-derived middle adjective, an Old English time noun, and the twin compound built on time.
intro.cn: 这个词由拉丁来源的「中间」形容词、古英语的时间名词，以及以 time 构成的孪生复合词共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: The first half of the compound goes back to Latin medianus, so the word carries one genuine Latin cognate inside it.
latinIntro.cn: 这个复合词的前半部分可追溯到拉丁语 medianus，因此词内确实含有一个拉丁同源成分。

definition_zh: 测量；量出；尺寸；措施；分寸；程度；节拍；格律
definition_en: to find the size or amount of something; a step taken to deal with a problem; a standard or a degree of something
core_image: 一把卷尺贴住桌沿，读出的数字被写进料单，旁边压着一张应对步骤的便签
scene: 木工把卷尺贴住桌沿，读出长度，再把数字写在料单上。Carpenters measure every board twice before the saw is switched on.
sceneCN: 这里取第 1 个义项：测定某物的尺寸或数量；句意为木工在开锯之前把每块板量两遍。图中可辨识物件：卷尺、桌沿、料单、铅笔；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 尺寸；量度；措施；分寸；（音乐的）小节；格律

senses.title: To find a size or amount
senses.definition: to find the size, length, weight or amount of something by using a tool or a standard
senses.definitionCN: 用工具或标准求出某物的尺寸、长度、重量或数量
senses.example: Carpenters measure every board twice before the saw is switched on.
senses.exampleCN: 木工在开锯之前把每块板量两遍。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to measure, and the physical act of comparing against a standard is the oldest sense.
senses.whyCN: 那个拉丁动词本意就是测量，拿某物与标准相比较的实体动作是最古老的一层。

senses.title: The number obtained
senses.definition: the size or amount that a measurement produces, often written as a figure with a unit
senses.definitionCN: 测量得出的尺寸或数量，常写成带单位的数字
senses.example: The measure came out at two metres, not one.
senses.exampleCN: 量出来的结果是一点九米，不是一米。
senses.why: A measurement is both the act and its outcome, so the noun carries the number as well as the procedure.
senses.whyCN: 测量既是动作也是结果，因此这个名词既携带数字，也携带过程。

senses.title: A step taken to fix something
senses.titleCN: 为解决问题所采取的步骤
senses.definition: an action or policy adopted to deal with a problem or to reach an aim
senses.definitionCN: 为处理问题或达到目的而采取的行动或政策
senses.example: The city took measures to cut traffic at the school gate.
senses.exampleCN: 市里采取措施减少校门口的交通。
senses.why: A step is a measured amount of action: enough to change the situation, not more, and the metaphor runs from dose to policy.
senses.whyCN: 一个步骤就是定量的行动：足以改变局面，又不过量，这个比喻从剂量一直走到政策。

senses.title: A proposed law
senses.definition: in a legislature, a proposed law put forward for debate and vote
senses.definitionCN: 在立法机构中提交辩论与表决的法律草案
senses.example: The measure passed by three votes.
senses.exampleCN: 这项法案以三票之差通过。
senses.why: A bill is a measured response written into legal form, and American usage kept the word for the draft itself.
senses.whyCN: 法案是把有分寸的应对写成法律形式，美式用法保留了这个词来指草案本身。

senses.title: A standard for comparison
senses.definition: a standard, unit or benchmark by which other things are judged
senses.definitionCN: 用来判断其他事物的标准、单位或基准
senses.example: Test scores are a crude measure of a school.
senses.exampleCN: 考试分数是对学校的一种粗略衡量。
senses.why: To measure anything one needs a fixed unit, and the noun then names any yardstick, including an abstract one.
senses.whyCN: 要测量任何东西都需要固定单位，名词随后指任何标尺，包括抽象的标尺。

senses.title: A degree or extent
senses.definition: the extent to which something is true or present, as in in large measure
senses.definitionCN: 某事物为真或存在的程度，如「在很大程度上」
senses.example: The success was in large measure due to the technicians.
senses.exampleCN: 这次成功在很大程度上要归功于技术人员。
senses.why: An amount can be spoken of without a ruler, so the word extends from physical quantity to degree of influence.
senses.whyCN: 数量可以不用尺子来说，于是这个词从物理量扩展到影响的程度。

senses.title: A limit or moderation
senses.definition: a proper limit in behaviour or feeling, or the absence of one in beyond measure
senses.definitionCN: 行为或情感上应有的限度，或在「无法估量」中表示没有限度
senses.example: His anger went beyond measure.
senses.exampleCN: 他的愤怒到了无法估量的地步。
senses.why: The idea of a fixed amount turns moral: to keep measure is to keep within bounds, and to exceed it is to lose proportion.
senses.whyCN: 固定数量的观念转向道德：守分寸就是守在界限内，越过就是失去比例。

senses.title: A bar in music
senses.definition: a group of beats between two bar lines, the unit of musical time
senses.definitionCN: 两条小节线之间的一组拍子，是音乐时间的基本单位
senses.example: The phrase fits one measure of four beats.
senses.exampleCN: 这个乐句正好占一小节四拍。
senses.why: Music divides time into equal measured spans, so the word for measuring became the name of the span.
senses.whyCN: 音乐把时间分成等长的段，于是表示测量的词成了那一段的名字。

senses.title: The metre of a line
senses.definition: the patterned rhythm of a line of verse, counted in feet
senses.definitionCN: 诗句中有规律的节奏，以音步计数
senses.example: The poem keeps a steady measure through twelve lines.
senses.exampleCN: 这首诗十二行都保持稳定的格律。
senses.why: Verse counts syllables the way a ruler counts inches, and the noun for the count became the name of the pattern.
senses.whyCN: 诗句像尺子量英寸那样数音节，表示计数的名词就成了这种模式的名字。

intro.en: Measure comes from Old French mesure, from Latin mensura 'a measuring', built on metiri 'to measure'. The root is generally connected with a very old word for measure that also gave Greek metron and English metre.
intro.cn: measure 来自古法语 mesure，源头是拉丁语 mensura「测量」，由 metiri「测量」构成。这个词根一般认为与一个极古老的「度量」词相关，希腊语 metron 与英语 metre 也出自它。

items.en: Metiri meant to measure or apportion, and it is the verb behind the whole family.
items.cn: metiri 意为测量、按量分配，是整个词族背后的动词。

items.en: Mensura named the act and the result of measuring, and it passed through French as the English noun.
items.cn: mensura 指测量的动作与结果，经法语成为英语名词。

items.en: The old root is generally reconstructed as a word for measure, the same one behind metre and metric; the reconstruction is accepted but the exact shape is source uncertain.
items.cn: 这个古老词根一般被重构为表示「度量」的词，metre 与 metric 也出自它；这一重构被接受，但确切形态来源不确定。

items.en: Old French mesure carried both the physical and the moral senses, and English took the pair together in the thirteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语 mesure 同时带有物理与道德两层意思，英语在十三世纪把两者一起接收。

items.en: American usage of the eighteenth century applied measure to a proposed law, a use that British English largely dropped.
items.cn: 十八世纪的美式用法把这个词用到法律草案上，英式英语后来大体放弃了这一用法。

items.en: Latin mensura had already named the counted span in rhythm, and English kept measure for a bar and for metrical pattern.
items.cn: 拉丁语 mensura 早已用来指节奏中被数出的段落，英语保留 measure 指小节与格律。

note.en: The first group shares the measuring root; the second group names related actions or quantities.
note.cn: 第一组共享「测量」词根；第二组是相关动作或数量。

entries.definition: The act or the figure produced by measuring.
entries.definitionCN: 测量的动作，或测量得出的数字。

entries.definition: Large or stable enough to be measured.
entries.definitionCN: 大到或稳定到可以被测量的。

entries.definition: Deliberate and restrained, as if each step were weighed.
entries.definitionCN: 审慎而有节制的，仿佛每一步都称过。

entries.definition: The process, or a compound for a tool such as a measuring tape.
entries.definitionCN: 测量过程，或构成卷尺一类工具名。

entries.definition: The mathematics of lengths, areas and volumes; a learned doublet.
entries.definitionCN: 研究长度、面积与体积的数学；学术性的同源词。

entries.definition: To estimate or measure, often with an instrument; also the instrument.
entries.definitionCN: 估计或测量，常借助仪器；也指该仪器。

entries.definition: To express something as a number.
entries.definitionCN: 把某事物表示为数字。

entries.definition: To judge the value or level of something, with less emphasis on units.
entries.definitionCN: 判断某物的价值或水平，对单位的强调较少。

entries.definition: An action taken toward a goal, the everyday word behind the policy sense.
entries.definitionCN: 为达到目标而采取的行动，是政策义背后的日常说法。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the Latin measuring verb, the real family and the fixed phrases of policy and tools.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用拉丁语测量动词、真实同族词，以及政策与工具里的固定搭配。

normal.en: Latin metiri meant to measure, and mensura gave English the noun through French.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 metiri 意为测量，mensura 经法语给了英语这个名词。

normal.en: The family runs measure, measurement, measurable, measured and measuring.
normal.cn: 同族词有 measure、measurement、measurable、measured 与 measuring。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the range: take measures, safety measures, in large measure, beyond measure.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出范围：采取措施、安全措施、在很大程度上、无法估量地。

normal.en: A tape measure is the tool, and a measure of success is the standard: one word, two kinds of ruler.
normal.cn: 卷尺是工具，衡量成功的标准是标尺：同一个词，两种尺。

normal.en: Music counts beats into a measure, and verse counts feet into a measure.
normal.cn: 音乐把拍子数成小节，诗句把音步数成格律。

abstract.en: To keep measure is to know how much is enough, which is a moral skill before it is a mathematical one.
abstract.cn: 守分寸就是知道多少算够，这先是道德的技能，然后才是数学的。

abstract.en: What can be measured is not always what matters, and what matters is not always measurable.
abstract.cn: 可测量的不总是重要的，重要的也不总是可测量的。

abstract.en: A measure is a decision about what counts, made before any number appears.
abstract.cn: 尺度是在数字出现之前，关于「什么算数」的决定。

examples.en: The nurse measured the wound and wrote the figure in the chart.
examples.cn: 护士量了伤口的大小，把数字写进病历。

examples.en: The council adopted three measures to reduce waste.
examples.cn: 议会通过三项措施减少浪费。

examples.en: Her patience was tested beyond measure that afternoon.
examples.cn: 那天下午，她的耐心受到了无法估量的考验。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「米热」——用尺子一点点比过去，看看到底有多长：测量

root: 拉丁语 metiri「测量」→ mensura「测量、量度」→ 古法语 mesure → 英语 measure。词根一般认为与古希腊语 metron 同源，确切形态属重构，来源不确定；法案、小节与格律义均为后起扩展。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one ruler: the act of measuring, the number it gives, a policy step, a bill, a standard, a degree of influence, a moral limit, a musical bar and a line's metre.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项跟着同一把尺：测量的动作、量出的数字、政策步骤、法案、比较标准、影响程度、道德限度、音乐小节与诗句格律。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tape is laid along the desk, and the number goes straight onto the cutting list.
core.cn: 核心意象：卷尺贴住桌沿，数字直接写进下料单。

branches.en: THE ACT AND THE FIGURE: laying a tape down, and the number that comes back.
branches.cn: 动作与数字：把尺子贴上去，以及报回来的那个数。

branches.en: THE POLICY DOSE: a step sized to the problem, and the same step written as a bill.
branches.cn: 政策剂量：按问题大小配出的步骤，以及写成法案的同一步骤。

branches.en: THE YARDSTICK: test scores used as a crude ruler for a school.
branches.cn: 标尺：把考试分数当作衡量学校的粗尺。

branches.en: THE DEGREE AND THE LIMIT: influence measured in large part, anger that passes all bounds.
branches.cn: 程度与限度：占很大部分的影响，与越过一切界限的愤怒。

branches.en: THE COUNTED SPAN: four beats between two bar lines, feet counted through a line of verse.
branches.cn: 被数出的段落：两条小节线之间的四拍，与一行诗里数出的音步。

intro.en: Measure is a Latin noun and verb of measuring, and the family keeps both the physical tool and the abstract standard.
intro.cn: measure 是拉丁语中表示测量的名词与动词，其词族同时保留实体工具与抽象标准两面。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is metiri, mensura and the adjective mensurabilis, with French mesure as the carrier into English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语成分是 metiri、mensura 与形容词 mensurabilis，古法语 mesure 则是进入英语的载体。

items.example: The noun carries both the act and the standard.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词同时携带动作与标准。

items.example: The verb is the root of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是整个词族的根。

items.example: It named both the act and its result.
items.exampleCN: 它兼指动作与结果。

items.example: It builds nouns of outcome, as in mensura.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示结果的词，如 mensura。

items.example: French added the moral sense of keeping within bounds.
items.exampleCN: 法语加上了守界限的道德含义。

items.meaning: the act or result of measuring
items.example: The English suffix names the process.
items.exampleCN: 英语词尾命名过程。
词尾表示可能。

items.example: The participle turned the noun into a manner.
items.exampleCN: 分词把名词变成了举止。

items.example: The negative suffix marks what cannot be counted.
items.exampleCN: 否定词尾标出无法计数之物。

items.example: The learned doublet stays close to Latin.
items.exampleCN: 这个学术同源词紧贴拉丁语。

latinEntries.example: Latin metiri means to measure or allot.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 metiri 意为测量、分配。

latinEntries.structure: Latin noun suffix -ura (result of an action)

senses.title: The act of measuring: taking a reading
senses.definition: the act or process of finding the size, amount or extent of something with an instrument
senses.definitionCN: 用仪器求出某物大小、数量或延展的过程
senses.example: Careful measurement of the sample took an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 仔细测量这个样本花了一小时。
senses.why: The suffix -ment, from Latin -mentum, names the act or its product. This first sense keeps the act: the tape is stretched and a value is sought.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ment 出自拉丁语 -mentum，表示动作或其产物。第一个义项保留动作义：卷尺被拉开，人们要找一个数值。

senses.title: The result: a figure or size obtained
senses.titleCN: 测量结果：得到的数字或尺寸
senses.definition: the figure, size or amount obtained by measuring
senses.definitionCN: 测量得到的数字、尺寸或数量
senses.example: The measurements show a room of about thirty square metres.
senses.exampleCN: 测量结果显示这个房间约三十平方米。
senses.why: The same suffix also names what the act leaves behind. Once the tape is folded away, the number remains, and that number is also called a measurement.
senses.whyCN: 同一个后缀也指动作留下的东西。卷尺收起来之后，数字仍然在，这个数字同样叫 measurement。

senses.title: A system of units used for measuring
senses.titleCN: 度量体系：用于测量的单位系统
senses.definition: a system of units and standards by which quantities are expressed, such as the metric system
senses.definitionCN: 用于表示数量的单位与标准体系，如公制
senses.example: The laboratory converted all readings to the metric system of measurement.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室把所有读数都换算成公制计量体系。
senses.why: A number means nothing without a unit. The word therefore also names the shared scale itself, the system that makes readings comparable between labs and countries.
senses.whyCN: 没有单位，数字毫无意义。因此这个词也指共享的尺度本身，即让不同实验室、不同国家的读数可以互比的那套体系。

senses.title: The method or instrument used to measure
senses.titleCN: 测定方法：用何种手段量
senses.definition: the technique or instrument by which a quantity is determined, as in a measurement technique
senses.definitionCN: 确定某一数量的技术或仪器，如某种测量技术
senses.example: They changed the measurement method to reduce noise in the data.
senses.exampleCN: 他们改换了测量方法以减少数据中的噪声。
senses.why: The word moves from the act to the means of the act. Asking about 'the measurement used' is asking which procedure produced the number.
senses.whyCN: 词从动作转到动作的手段。问「用的是什么测量」，问的就是哪个流程产出了这个数字。

senses.title: Assessment: measuring performance or quality
senses.titleCN: 评估：把表现或质量当成量来测
senses.definition: the assessment of performance, quality or progress as if it were a quantity
senses.definitionCN: 把表现、质量或进展当作数量来评估
senses.example: Measurement of teacher performance is itself controversial.
senses.exampleCN: 对教师表现的评估本身就很有争议。
senses.why: What cannot be held with a tape can still be treated as a quantity. The word extends from physical size to judgement, and keeps the authority of the instrument.
senses.whyCN: 卷尺量不了的东西仍可被当作数量来处理。这个词从物理尺寸延伸到判断，同时保留了仪器的权威感。

senses.title: Body measurements: sizes taken for clothing
senses.titleCN: 身体尺寸：做衣服时量的三围
senses.definition: the set of body sizes taken with a tape, used for making or buying clothes
senses.definitionCN: 用软尺量出的一组身体尺寸，用于做衣或买衣
senses.example: The tailor took my measurements before cutting the cloth.
senses.exampleCN: 裁缝在裁布之前先量了我的尺寸。
senses.why: Here measurements is plural because a body yields several figures. The word keeps its plain physical sense but names a set rather than a single value.
senses.whyCN: 这里用复数，因为一具身体会得到好几个数字。词仍保留朴素的物理义，只是指一组值而非单个值。

senses.title: Precision measurement: readings and their error
senses.titleCN: 精密计量：读数与它的误差
senses.definition: the technical process of obtaining precise values, considered together with instrument error and uncertainty
senses.definitionCN: 获得精确数值的技术过程，并连同仪器误差与不确定度一起考虑
senses.example: Every measurement carries an uncertainty that must be reported.
senses.exampleCN: 每次测量都带有一个必须报告的不确定度。
senses.why: In metrology the word names a physical process with limits. Since no instrument is perfect, a measurement is always a value plus an admitted range of doubt.
senses.whyCN: 在计量学中，这个词指一个有极限的物理过程。仪器都不完美，所以测量永远是数值加上一个被承认的误差范围。

senses.title: Recorded readings: the data set
senses.titleCN: 测量数据：记录下来的一整套读数
senses.definition: the recorded set of readings taken during an experiment or survey
senses.definitionCN: 在一次实验或调查中记录下来的一整套读数
senses.example: The raw measurements were stored before any analysis.
senses.exampleCN: 原始测量数据在任何分析之前先被存了下来。
senses.why: Once readings are written down they become data. The plural then names a collection, and the word sits between the act of measuring and the analysis that follows.
senses.whyCN: 读数一旦写下就成了数据。复数于是指一个集合，而这个词正处在测量动作与随后分析之间的位置上。

intro.en: Measurement is the English noun measure plus -ment, from Latin -mentum, which names an act or its result. Measure came into English in the 14th century through Old French mesure from Latin mensura, the noun of metiri 'to measure'. The compound measurement is recorded in the 18th century, when scientific instruments made repeated readings a routine matter. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: measurement 是英语名词 measure 加 -ment，后者出自拉丁语 -mentum，表示动作或其结果。measure 在 14 世纪经古法语 mesure 进入英语，源自拉丁语 mensura，即 metiri「测量」的名词。measurement 这一复合形式在 18 世纪见于记载，当时科学仪器使反复读数成为常规。年代为大致估计。

items.en: Metric conventions and national standards bureaus make measurement a public, regulated activity rather than a craftsman's habit.
items.cn: 公制惯例与各国标准局的建立，使测量从工匠的习惯变成公共的、受规范的活动。

items.en: English measurement is recorded, formed from measure plus -ment as instruments and experiments spread.
items.cn: 英语 measurement 见于记载，随仪器与实验的普及由 measure 加 -ment 构成。

items.en: measure is borrowed through Old French mesure and covers a unit, a limit and the act of measuring.
items.cn: measure 经古法语 mesure 借入，兼指单位、限度与测量行为。

items.en: mensura is the noun of metiri; the same verb gives dimension, commensurate and immense.
items.cn: mensura 是 metiri 的名词形式；同一个动词还给出 dimension、commensurate、immense。

items.en: metiri rests on the reconstructed root *med- 'to measure, take the right size', which also gives modus and hence mode and moderate.
items.cn: metiri 建立在重构词根 *med-「测量、取恰当尺寸」上，该词根也给出 modus，进而有 mode 与 moderate。

note.en: The first group separates true relatives from a word that merely looks technical; the second compares words used in neighbouring parts of the same task.
note.cn: 第一组把真正的同族词与只是看起来专业的词分开；第二组比较同一件事相邻环节上的词。

entries.definition: the verb 'to find the size of' and the noun for a unit, limit or legislative step. Measurement is only the act or result, while measure also names the standard and the policy.
entries.definitionCN: 动词「测量」，名词指单位、限度或立法措施。measurement 只指动作或结果，而 measure 还指标准与政策措施。

entries.definition: the branch of geometry dealing with lengths, areas and volumes, or the act of measuring in a formal sense. It is the learned Latin-style counterpart, confined to technical writing.
entries.definitionCN: 研究长度、面积与体积的几何分支，或正式意义上的测量行为。它是学术性的拉丁式对应词，只用于技术写作。

entries.definition: a measurable extent such as length, width or height. It comes from dis- plus metiri, so it shares the measuring verb but names an extent rather than the act of measuring it.
entries.definitionCN: 可测量的延展，如长、宽、高。它由 dis- 加 metiri 构成，共享「测量」这个动词，但指延展本身，而不是测量的动作。

entries.definition: the act of judging the value or quality of something. It overlaps the figurative sense of measurement but does not require numbers.
entries.definitionCN: 对某物价值或质量的判断。它与 measurement 的引申义重叠，但不要求有数字。

entries.definition: the figure shown by an instrument at a moment. It is one measurement in the narrowest sense, taken off a dial or a display.
entries.definitionCN: 仪器在某一刻显示的数字。它是最狭义的一次测量，取自表盘或显示屏。

entries.definition: a defined indicator used to judge performance. It is a measurement chosen for a purpose, where measurement is the general obtaining of values.
entries.definitionCN: 用于评判表现的确定指标。它是为某个目的选定的测量，而 measurement 是一般的取值过程。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real pieces of the word and its real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想只使用这个词真实的构成成分和真实同族词，不用编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: -ment gives both faces of the word: the act of measuring and the figure that the act leaves behind.
normal.cn: -ment 给出这个词的两面：测量的动作，以及动作留下的数字。

normal.en: measure is the verb and the general noun; measurement is specifically the act or the result, never the policy.
normal.cn: measure 是动词兼一般名词；measurement 专指动作或结果，从不指政策措施。

normal.en: A measurement without a unit is just a number, which is why the word also names the system of units.
normal.cn: 没有单位的测量只是一个数字，所以这个词也指单位体系。

normal.en: The plural measurements usually means a set: body sizes, or a table of readings from an experiment.
normal.cn: 复数 measurements 通常指一个集合：身体尺寸，或实验读出的一整表数值。

normal.en: Measurement error is not a mistake but the admitted uncertainty that comes with every instrument.
normal.cn: measurement error（测量误差）不是错误，而是每件仪器都带来的、被承认的不确定度。

abstract.en: See a tape stretched, a number written, and a unit agreed: the three parts of every measurement.
abstract.cn: 想象卷尺拉开、数字写下、单位约定：这就是每次测量的三个部分。

abstract.en: The word travels from hand to page to report, and loses nothing but gains a claim to objectivity.
abstract.cn: 这个词从手上走到纸面再走到报告，什么也没丢，却获得了一种客观性的主张。

abstract.en: Whenever someone says 'by measurement', ask which instrument and which unit did the speaking.
abstract.cn: 每当有人说「按测量」，就该问：是哪件仪器、哪个单位在说话。

examples.en: Repeated measurement reduced the effect of random error.
examples.cn: 反复测量减小了随机误差的影响。

examples.en: The engineer sent the measurements to the factory.
examples.cn: 工程师把尺寸数据发给了工厂。

examples.en: Their claim rests on a single measurement taken at noon.
examples.cn: 他们的结论建立在正午所做的一次测量上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「没辙门特」——没辙时也得把门特（门）量一遍 → measurement 测量、尺寸

root: 拉丁语 metiri「测量」→ mensura「尺度」→ 古法语 mesure → 英语 measure；加 -ment（拉丁 -mentum，表示动作或结果）→ measurement。核心是「量这一动作，以及量出来的那个数」。

sensesIntro.en: All eight senses keep one image: a tape pulled across something. What changes is which part of the event is named — the pulling, the number, the agreed unit, the method, the judgement, the body being fitted, the error, or the whole table of readings.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都保留同一个意象：一条卷尺拉过某物。变化的只是命名了这件事的哪一段——拉尺的动作、数字、约定的单位、方法、判断、被量身的身体、误差，还是整张读数表。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a carpenter's tape stretched across a board, the figure written down.
core.cn: 核心意象：木匠的卷尺拉过木板，数字被写下来。

branches.en: THE ACT: the tape is stretched and a value is sought, which is measuring as an activity.
branches.cn: 动作：卷尺拉开去找一个值，这就是作为活动的测量。

branches.en: THE PRODUCT: one figure, or the whole recorded table of figures left after the act.
branches.cn: 产物：单个数字，或动作结束后留下的整张记录表。

branches.en: THE SHARED SCALE: units and standards make one lab's number comparable with another's.
branches.cn: 共享尺度：单位与标准让一个实验室的数字可与另一个实验室的比较。

branches.en: THE INSTRUMENT AND ITS LIMIT: the method produces the value, and every method brings its own uncertainty.
branches.cn: 仪器及其极限：方法产出数值，而每种方法都带来自己的不确定度。

branches.en: THE BODY AND THE JUDGEMENT: sizes taken for a suit, and performance treated as if it could be measured.
branches.cn: 身体与判断：为做衣量出的尺寸，以及被当作可测量的表现。

intro.en: Measurement is measure plus -ment, from Latin -mentum. That suffix names an act (as in movement) or its result (as in document), and measurement uses both faces.
intro.cn: measurement 是 measure 加 -ment，出自拉丁语 -mentum。这个后缀表示动作（如 movement「移动」）或其结果（如 document「文件」），measurement 两面都用上了。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is metiri 'to measure' with its noun mensura. The suffix -mentum also appears in document, monument and argument.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词基是 metiri「测量」及其名词 mensura。后缀 -mentum 也见于 document「文件」、monument「纪念碑」、argument「论点」。

items.meaning: the act of measuring, or the figure obtained
items.example: The measurement was repeated three times.
items.exampleCN: 这次测量重复了三遍。

items.meaning: to find the size of, or a unit, limit or step
items.meaningCN: 测量；亦指单位、限度或措施
items.example: They measured the depth of the well.
items.exampleCN: 他们量了井的深度。

items.example: The gain was measurable within a month.
items.exampleCN: 一个月内就有了可测的增益。
房间明显安静了下来。

items.example: The measurability of pain is limited.
items.exampleCN: 疼痛的可测性是有限的。

items.meaning: having no limits that can be measured
items.meaningCN: 无边无际的；无法计量的
items.exampleCN: 他们穿过一片无边无际的平原。

items.structure: the same noun used for the technical process
items.meaning: the regulated process of obtaining values with instruments
items.meaningCN: 用仪器取得数值的规范过程
items.exampleCN: 测量标准保护着贸易。

items.meaning: the formal or geometric measuring of lengths, areas and volumes
items.meaningCN: 测量术；几何中的长度面积体积计算
items.example: Mensuration is taught with areas and volumes.
items.exampleCN: 测量术是随面积与体积一起教的。

items.meaning: a measured extent such as length
items.example: Length is one dimension of the box.
items.exampleCN: 长度是这个箱子的一个维度。

items.meaning: measured by the same standard, and so proportionate
items.example: The fine was commensurate with the damage.
items.exampleCN: 罚款与损害程度相称。

latinEntries.meaning: forms nouns of action or result
latinEntries.meaningCN: 构成表示动作或结果的名词

definition_zh: 肉；食用肉；（果实或坚果的）可食部分；实质；要旨
definition_en: the flesh of animals eaten as food, the soft edible part inside fruit or nuts, or the central substance of something
core_image: 一块放在砧板上的肉，旁边是敲开的坚果，露出里面饱满的果仁
scene: 冬天的炖锅在灶上咕嘟作响，屋里飘着香料味。She added a little salt to the meat and left it to simmer.
sceneCN: 这里是「供食用的肉」（第 1 个义项：动物肉作为食物）；句意为她往肉里加了一点盐，让它慢慢炖。

derivatives.zh: 由 meat 加形容词后缀 -y 构成，义为「多肉的；内容丰富的」
由 meat 加否定后缀 -less 构成，义为「无肉的」
由 meat 与 ball 复合而成，义为「肉丸」

senses.title: Animal flesh used as food
senses.definition: the flesh of animals, especially cattle, pigs and sheep, eaten as food
senses.definitionCN: 尤指牛、猪、羊等动物供人食用的肉
senses.example: The butcher cut the meat into thin slices.
senses.exampleCN: 屠夫把肉切成薄片。
senses.why: Old English mete meant food of any kind; as other foods took their own names, the general word narrowed onto the flesh sold at a butcher's stall.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 mete 泛指任何食物；随着其他食物各自有了名字，这个宽泛的词就收窄到肉铺案板上出售的肉。

senses.title: The edible soft part of fruit or nuts
senses.definition: the soft or fleshy part inside a fruit, nut or shell that can be eaten
senses.definitionCN: 水果、坚果或壳内可供食用的柔软部分
senses.example: Crack the shell and scoop out the meat of the walnut.
senses.exampleCN: 敲开壳，把核桃仁挖出来。
senses.why: The idea of the edible inside of a thing was already present in food, so the word was extended to the part of a nut or fruit worth eating.
senses.whyCN: 「某物内部可食的部分」这一想法本就包含在「食物」里，于是词义被扩展到坚果或水果里值得吃的那一部分。

senses.title: The central substance of an idea or text
senses.definition: the most important part or central content of an argument, book or plan
senses.definitionCN: 论点、书或计划中最重要的部分、核心内容
senses.example: The meat of the report is in its final three pages.
senses.exampleCN: 报告的要旨就在最后三页。
senses.why: If flesh is what fills a body, then the substantial part of a text can be called its meat, with the rest treated as bone or wrapping.
senses.whyCN: 如果肉是填满身体的东西，那么一篇文章的实质部分也可以叫它的 meat，其余部分则被看成骨头或包装。

senses.title: Food of any kind, in older usage
senses.definition: solid food in general, the older sense still visible in a few fixed phrases
senses.definitionCN: 泛指固体食物，这一较古的词义仍残留在少数固定短语中
senses.example: In older English, meat could mean any food a household stored.
senses.exampleCN: 在较早的英语里，meat 可以指一户人家储存的任何食物。
senses.why: This is the original sense; it survives mainly in old texts and in the fixed phrase meat and drink, while everyday usage keeps only the flesh sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最初的词义；它主要残存在旧文本与固定短语 meat and drink 里，日常用法只保留了「肉」这一义项。

intro.en: Meat began as a general word for food and narrowed to animal flesh, a shift whose exact cause is not settled.
intro.cn: meat 起初是泛指食物的词，后来收窄为动物肉，这一变化的确切原因尚无定论。

items.en: The reconstructed noun *matiz meant food, and its earlier origin is uncertain; no reliable Latin cognate is recorded.
items.cn: 重构名词 *matiz 意为食物，其更早的来源不确定，也没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.en: Old English mete meant food or nourishment of any kind, not flesh in particular.
items.cn: 古英语 mete 泛指食物或营养，并不专指肉。

items.en: Middle English kept the broad sense, and meat could still name bread, fruit or drink in the same sentence.
items.cn: 中古英语保留宽泛的词义，meat 仍可与面包、水果或饮料并列。

items.en: Usage narrowed towards animal flesh, though scholars do not agree on a single cause for the change.
items.cn: 词义逐渐收窄到动物肉，不过学者对变化的确切原因并无一致结论。

items.en: The flesh sense dominates, while the older idea survives in compounds and in the figurative sense of substance.
items.cn: 「肉」的义项占主导，较古的词义则保存在复合词与「实质」的比喻义里。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the flesh family and one word that merely sounds the same; the near-meaning group collects names for flesh and for kinds of meat.
note.cn: 形近组收「肉」这一族词，外加一个只是读音相同的词；近义组收表示肉与各种肉类的词。

entries.definition: The soft body tissue of a person or animal.
entries.definitionCN: 人或动物身上的软组织。

entries.definitionCN: 牛肉，一种具体的红肉。

entries.definition: Meat from pigs.
entries.definitionCN: 猪肉。

entries.definition: Wild animals hunted for food, or their meat.
entries.definitionCN: 供食用的野味或其肉。

normalIntro.en: The word started wide and ended narrow, and the old width still shows in a few compounds and in the sense of substance.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从宽泛起步、以狭窄收场，旧日的宽泛仍体现在少数复合词与「实质」义里。

normal.en: Old English mete was a general word for food, so the ancestor of meat had nothing to do with animals.
normal.cn: 古英语 mete 是泛指食物的词，所以 meat 的祖先与动物无关。

normal.en: The narrowing to flesh happened gradually, and nobody can point to one single cause.
normal.cn: 收窄为「肉」是逐渐发生的，没有人能指出唯一的原因。

normal.en: The adjective meaty adds -y, and meatless adds -less, two small endings that show the flesh sense clearly.
normal.cn: 形容词 meaty 加 -y，meatless 加 -less，两个小后缀清楚显示了「肉」的义项。

normal.en: Meatball is a plain compound: meat plus ball, the shape named directly.
normal.cn: meatball 是直白的复合词：meat 加 ball，直接以形状命名。

normal.en: The meat of a walnut or the meat of an argument keeps the old idea of the edible or substantial inside.
normal.cn: 核桃的 meat 或论点的 meat，都保留了「内部可食或实质部分」的旧想法。

abstract.en: Picture a butcher's block: the word food shrank until it fit exactly on that block.
abstract.cn: 想象一块肉铺的砧板：food 这个词不断缩小，直到正好落在砧板上。

abstract.en: Every language has words that start wide and end narrow, and meat is one of the clearest examples.
abstract.cn: 每种语言都有由宽变窄的词，meat 就是最清楚的例子之一。

abstract.en: Cut a nut open and the same word appears again, this time for the good part inside.
abstract.cn: 把坚果切开，同一个词又出现了，这次指里面最好的那部分。

examples.en: She added a little salt to the meat and left it to simmer.
examples.cn: 她往肉里加了一点盐，让它慢慢炖。

examples.en: The butcher cut the meat into thin slices.
examples.cn: 屠夫把肉切成薄片。

examples.en: The meat of the report is in its final three pages.
examples.cn: 报告的要旨就在最后三页。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the edible part of a body; the senses move from animal flesh to the inside of a nut and finally to the substance of an argument.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是身体上可食的部分；义项从动物肉移到坚果内部，最后移到论点的实质。

senses.title: A person who repairs machines
senses.definition: a person whose job is to repair and maintain machines, especially the engines of cars
senses.definitionCN: 以修理和保养机器为职业的人，尤指修汽车发动机的人
senses.example: The mechanic found the leak within ten minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 机修工十分钟内就找到了漏点。
senses.why: Greek mekhane named a device or machine, and the ending that marks a person turned the idea of machinery into the craftsperson who keeps it running.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 mekhane 指装置、机械，加上表示「从事某事的人」的词尾，就把「机械」变成了让它保持运转的手艺人。

senses.title: The science of motion and forces
senses.definition: the branch of science that studies how forces move bodies, usually written as mechanics
senses.definitionCN: 研究力如何使物体运动的科学分支，通常写作 mechanics
senses.example: The old textbooks called the study of forces mechanic, a name now usually replaced by mechanics.
senses.exampleCN: 旧课本把研究力的学问称作 mechanic，如今通常改用 mechanics。
senses.why: The same Greek root named the machine and the knowledge of how it moves, so the science of forces kept the singular form in older English usage.
senses.whyCN: 同一个希腊词根既指机械，也指关于它如何运动的知识，所以研究力的学问在较早的英语里保留了单数形式。

senses.title: A skilled worker who builds or operates machinery
senses.definition: a skilled manual worker who makes, fits or operates machinery, a sense common in older industrial English
senses.definitionCN: 制造、装配或操作机械的熟练手工劳动者，这一义项在较早的工业英语中常见
senses.example: The factory hired a mechanic who could set up the new lathe.
senses.exampleCN: 工厂雇了一名会给新机床做调试的机械师。
senses.why: Before motor cars, mekhane covered any machine, so a mechanic was simply the person who understood and handled machinery of any kind.
senses.whyCN: 在汽车出现之前，mekhane 泛指任何机械，因此 mechanic 就是懂机械、会摆弄机械的人，不限种类。

senses.title: Someone good at handling tools and devices
senses.definition: in informal use, a person who is unusually good at making things work or at handling tools and devices
senses.definitionCN: 口语中指特别擅长让东西运转、或摆弄工具与器械的人
senses.example: Ask him to fix the printer; he is a real mechanic with anything that has gears.
senses.exampleCN: 让他去修打印机吧，凡是带齿轮的东西他都很在行。
senses.why: Because a mechanic must diagnose a machine by feel and sound, the word widened from a job title to praise for anyone with that practical touch.
senses.whyCN: 机修工必须凭手感和声音判断机器毛病，于是这个词从职业名称扩展为对任何有这种实用本领之人的称赞。

intro.en: Mechanic is a Greek word about machines that travelled through Latin and French before English used it for the person, the craft and the science of motion.
intro.cn: mechanic 是希腊语中与机械有关的词，经拉丁语与法语传入英语，先指懂机械的人，也指这门手艺与运动之学。

items.en: Mekhane meant a device, a tool or a machine, and it also carried the idea of a trick or a contrivance.
items.cn: mekhane 意为装置、工具或机械，也带有「巧计、机关」的意思。

items.en: The adjective mekhanikos described what belonged to machines and to inventing them, and it named the person who understood such things.
items.cn: 形容词 mekhanikos 描述属于机械、属于发明机械的事物，也用来称懂这类东西的人。

items.en: Latin borrowed the Greek word as mechanicus, an adjective and a noun for things and people concerned with machines.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入希腊词，作 mechanicus，既是形容词也作名词，指与机械有关的事物和人。

items.en: Old French used mecanique for the art of machines and for the science of motion, passing both senses toward English.
items.cn: 古法语用 mecanique 指机械技艺与运动之学，两种含义一起传向英语。

items.en: English kept mechanic for the person and mechanics for the science, while mechanical covers the adjective.
items.cn: 英语保留 mechanic 指人、mechanics 指力学，形容用法则由 mechanical 承担。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words built on the same Greek root for machines; the near-meaning group collects people who repair, design or operate them.
note.cn: 形近组收同一希腊词根上的机械词族；近义组收修理、设计或操作机器的人。

entries.definition: Worked by machinery or done without thought, like a machine.
entries.definitionCN: 由机械驱动的；或像机器一样不加思考的。

entries.definition: The science of motion and forces, or the working parts of a machine.
entries.definitionCN: 研究运动与力的科学；也指机器的运转部件。

entries.definition: The parts that make a machine work, or a process by which something happens.
entries.definitionCN: 使机器运转的部件；也指某事发生的机制。

entries.definition: To replace human or animal work with machines.
entries.definitionCN: 用机器取代人力或畜力。

entries.definition: A person trained to do practical work with equipment or instruments.
entries.definitionCN: 受过训练、会用设备或仪器做实际工作的人。

entries.definition: A person who designs, builds or maintains engines and structures.
entries.definitionCN: 设计、建造或维护发动机与工程结构的人。

entries.definition: A person whose job is to mend broken machines or equipment.
entries.definitionCN: 以修理坏掉的机器或设备为职业的人。

entries.definition: A person who operates a machine tool or makes machine parts.
entries.definitionCN: 操作机床或制作机器零件的人。

normalIntro.en: The word rests on a Greek noun for a machine; its family keeps returning to devices, their parts and the knowledge of how they move.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词建立在表示机械的希腊名词上，同族词反复回到装置、部件以及关于它们如何运动的知识。

normal.en: Mekhane in Greek is a machine or a device, so a mechanic is the person attached to a machine.
normal.cn: 希腊语 mekhane 是机械、装置，所以 mechanic 就是与机械绑在一起的那个人。

normal.en: The same root gives mechanics, the science of how machines and bodies move.
normal.cn: 同一词根还给出 mechanics，即研究机器与物体如何运动的力学。

normal.en: Mechanical adds -al and means working like a machine, even without thought.
normal.cn: mechanical 加 -al，意为像机器一样运转，甚至不加思考。

normal.en: Mechanism is the inside of the machine, the parts that produce the motion.
normal.cn: mechanism 指机器内部那些产生运动的部件。

normal.en: Mechanize means to put a machine where a hand used to be.
normal.cn: mechanize 意为把原来用手的地方换成机器。

abstract.en: A mechanic knows a machine by sound before opening it, which shows how much of repair is attention.
abstract.cn: 机修工在拆开之前就能凭声音判断机器，这说明修理很大一部分靠的是留意。

abstract.en: From one Greek word for device grow the person, the science and the inner parts, three views of the same thing.
abstract.cn: 从一个表示装置的希腊词长出人、科学与内部构造，这是同一件事的三种看法。

abstract.en: The word reminds us that every working machine is held together by somebody who listens to it.
abstract.cn: 这个词提醒人：每台能运转的机器背后，都有个在倾听它的人把它维持住。

examples.en: The mechanic traced the noise to a worn bearing.
examples.cn: 机修工把异响追查到一处磨损的轴承。

examples.en: Every mechanic in the shop knows that engine by sound.
examples.cn: 店里每个机修工都能凭声音认出那台发动机。

examples.en: A good mechanic listens before reaching for a wrench.
examples.cn: 好机修工先听，再伸手拿扳手。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「麦卡尼克」——听起来像被麦子卡住的人，其实他正钻在车底修车；记住 mechanic 是机修工。

root: 希腊语 mekhane（机械、装置）经 mekhanikos 进入拉丁语 mechanicus，再经法语进入英语；同族词多与机械、运动与构造有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the machine and the person who keeps it working; from that come the science of motion, the older industrial craftsman and the informal praise for a practical hand.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是机械以及让它保持运转的人；由此分出运动之学、较早的工业技工，以及对有实用本领者的口语称赞。

senses.title: Relating to machines
senses.definition: concerning machines or their parts rather than human or electronic action
senses.definitionCN: 涉及机器或其部件，而非人或电子动作
senses.example: A mechanical clock needs winding once a day.
senses.exampleCN: 机械钟每天要上一次发条。
senses.why: the adjective was built on the Greek word for a device, so its first job is to mark things of that kind.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词建在希腊语「装置」一词上，因此首要作用是标记同类事物。

senses.title: Of a machine's working parts
senses.definition: describing a fault or action that belongs to moving parts, not to power or software
senses.definitionCN: 描述属于运动部件的故障或动作，而非电力或软件
senses.example: The mechanic found a mechanical cause for the noise.
senses.exampleCN: 技工找到了噪声的机械原因。
senses.why: when a system has layers, the adjective isolates the layer of gears, bearings and seals.
senses.whyCN: 当系统分层时，这个形容词专门标出齿轮、轴承与密封件那一层。

senses.title: Belonging to mechanics as a science
senses.definition: concerning the study of forces and motion rather than chemistry or electricity
senses.definitionCN: 涉及力与运动的研究，而非化学或电学
senses.example: The paper sits on the boundary between mechanical and electrical effects.
senses.exampleCN: 那篇论文处在力学效应与电学效应的交界上。
senses.why: the same Greek root names a branch of physics, and the adjective follows it into the classroom.
senses.whyCN: 同一个希腊词根也命名物理学的一个分支，形容词便随之进入课堂。

senses.title: Automatic, without thought
senses.definition: done by habit or rule with no attention behind it
senses.definitionCN: 凭习惯或规则完成，背后没有留意
senses.example: His apology sounded mechanical and convinced no one.
senses.exampleCN: 他的道歉听起来很机械，谁也没被说服。
senses.why: a machine repeats without judging, and human behaviour that repeats without judging borrows the word.
senses.whyCN: 机器重复而不判断，人不判断地重复行为时便借用这个词。

senses.title: Barely varying, routine
senses.titleCN: 几乎不变的、例行公事的
senses.definition: describing a process that repeats identically with no adjustment
senses.definitionCN: 描述一模一样重复、毫无调整的过程
senses.example: The grading was mechanical: same comments, different names.
senses.exampleCN: 那次评分很机械：评语都一样，只是名字不同。
senses.why: repetition without variation is the visible signature of a machine at work.
senses.whyCN: 毫无变化的重复，是机器运转时最显眼的特征。

senses.title: Describing a physical breakdown
senses.definition: used of a failure caused by wear, jam or breakage of parts
senses.definitionCN: 用于因磨损、卡死或断裂造成的失效
senses.example: Mechanical damage is cheaper to prevent than to repair.
senses.exampleCN: 机械损伤预防起来比修理便宜。
senses.why: engineers divide failures by cause, and this adjective labels the cause that lives in the hardware.
senses.whyCN: 工程师按原因给故障分类，这个形容词标记住在硬件里的那一类。

senses.title: Of mechanical advantage
senses.definition: concerning the ratio by which a tool multiplies force
senses.definitionCN: 涉及工具放大力量的比值
senses.example: A lever gives mechanical gain at the cost of distance.
senses.exampleCN: 杠杆以距离为代价换取机械上的增益。
senses.why: the science of mechanics measures how tools multiply force, and that measure carries the adjective.
senses.whyCN: 力学测量工具如何放大力量，这一测量便带着这个形容词。

senses.title: Of reproduction by machine
senses.definition: describing copies made by a device rather than by hand
senses.definitionCN: 描述由装置而非手工做出的复制
senses.example: Mechanical copies of the print are worth far less than the original.
senses.exampleCN: 那幅版画的机械复制品比原作便宜得多。
senses.why: the age of printed multiples made the word a standard label for copies a machine produces.
senses.whyCN: 印刷复制品的时代让这个词成了机器所产副本的标准标签。

senses.title: Of a device's touch and feel
senses.definition: describing switches or keys that act through physical parts
senses.definitionCN: 描述通过实体部件动作的开关或按键
senses.example: She still prefers a mechanical switch for typing.
senses.exampleCN: 打字时她仍偏爱机械开关。
senses.why: users distinguish a real moving part from a touch surface, and the old adjective draws the line.
senses.whyCN: 用户要区分真正的运动部件与触摸表面，旧形容词正好划出这条线。

senses.title: Drawn with instruments
senses.definition: describing technical drawing done with rulers and compasses rather than freehand
senses.definitionCN: 描述用直尺与圆规而非徒手完成的技术制图
senses.example: The old course began with mechanical drawing before design.
senses.exampleCN: 那门旧课程先教机械制图，再教设计。
senses.why: before printing, precision came from instruments, and drawing by instrument took the adjective's name.
senses.whyCN: 在印刷之前，精确来自仪器，用仪器绘图便取了这个形容词的名字。

intro.en: Mechanical comes from Greek mekhane, a device or means, through Latin mechanicus. The adjective first meant belonging to machines and later came to mean unthinking.
intro.cn: mechanical 来自希腊语 mekhane「装置、手段」，经拉丁语 mechanicus 而来。形容词最初指「属于机器的」，后来引申为「不加思考的」。

items.en: Greek mekhane meant a machine, a device or a means of doing something, and mekhos meant a means or expedient.
items.cn: 希腊语 mekhane 指机器、装置或做事的手段，mekhos 指手段或办法。

items.en: The adjective mekhanikos described what belongs to devices or to inventive skill.
items.cn: 形容词 mekhanikos 描述属于装置或属于巧思技艺的事物。

items.en: Latin mechanicus kept the Greek sense and was used of mechanical arts and of engineers.
items.cn: 拉丁语 mechanicus 保留希腊含义，用于机械技艺与工程人员。

items.en: English mechanical first meant of machines and of the science of mechanics, with no hint of dullness.
items.cn: 英语 mechanical 最初指机器与力学，还没有「呆板」的暗示。

items.en: Newtonian mechanics made the adjective the standard label for force and motion, and the noun mechanics followed.
items.cn: 牛顿力学让这个形容词成为力与运动的标准标签，名词 mechanics 随后出现。

items.en: Industry and bureaucracy made repetition visible, and the adjective acquired its modern meaning of acting without thought.
items.cn: 工业与官僚制度让重复变得显眼，这个形容词于是获得「不假思索」的现代含义。

note.en: The first group is the same machine root in other shapes; the second group is the neighbouring words for automatic and machine-made.
note.cn: 第一组是同一「机器」词根的其他形式；第二组是「自动」与「机器制造」的相邻说法。

entries.definition: One who repairs machines; the adjective describes what belongs to machines.
entries.definitionCN: 指修理机器的人；形容词描述属于机器的事物。

entries.definition: The study of forces and motion; the adjective's third sense points to it.
entries.definitionCN: 研究力与运动的学问；形容词的第三个义项指向它。

entries.definition: The assembly of parts that produces an action; the adjective describes such parts.
entries.definitionCN: 指产生某个动作的部件组合；形容词描述这类部件。

entries.definition: In a machine-like or unthinking way; it tells how something is done.
entries.definitionCN: 以机器般或不假思索的方式；它说明做事的方式。

entries.definition: Working by itself once set going; mechanical stresses the parts, automatic stresses the lack of a hand.
entries.definitionCN: 一旦启动便自行工作；mechanical 强调部件，automatic 强调不需人手。

entries.definition: Done with the hands; it is the direct opposite of mechanical action.
entries.definitionCN: 用手完成的；是机械动作的直接对立面。

entries.definition: Regular and unvarying; routine describes the pattern, mechanical describes the absence of thought.
entries.definitionCN: 规律而少变化；routine 描述模式，mechanical 描述缺少思考。

entries.definition: Stiff and emotionless in manner; a modern synonym for the figurative sense of mechanical.
entries.definitionCN: 举止僵硬而无感情；是 mechanical 比喻义的现代同义说法。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations from the real Greek root and the real technical phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：来自真实希腊词根与真实技术搭配。

normal.en: Mekhane is a device, so mechanical means device-like before it means unthinking.
normal.cn: mekhane 是装置，所以 mechanical 先表示「像装置的」，再表示「不假思索的」。

normal.en: The family is regular: mechanic, mechanics, mechanism, mechanically.
normal.cn: 词族很整齐：mechanic、mechanics、mechanism、mechanically。

normal.en: Fixed phrases split the senses: mechanical failure, mechanical advantage, mechanical repetition.
normal.cn: 固定搭配分开义项：机械故障、机械效益、机械的重复。

normal.en: The adverb ends in -ly, and the comparison uses more and most.
normal.cn: 副词以 -ly 结尾，比较级用 more 与 most。

normal.en: It contrasts with manual, which is the hand against the gear.
normal.cn: 它与 manual 相对：一只手对着一个齿轮。

abstract.en: Picture a gear with one tooth missing, still turning because nothing has told it to stop.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚缺了齿的齿轮还在转，因为没人告诉它该停。

abstract.en: Picture a hand that apologises on a schedule, never looking up.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手按时间表道歉，从不抬头。

abstract.en: Picture a drawing so straight that the ruler is still visible in the ink.
abstract.cn: 想象一张画得极直的图，墨迹里还看得见尺子。

examples.en: Mechanical wear, not bad code, caused the shutdown.
examples.cn: 造成停机的是机械磨损，而不是糟糕的代码。

examples.en: His replies were polite but entirely mechanical.
examples.cn: 他的回答礼貌，却完全是机械式的。

examples.en: Mechanical drawings from that era still guide the repair shop.
examples.cn: 那个年代的机械制图至今仍指导着修理车间。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「米（me）卡（cha）你扣（ni-cal）」——米粒卡住你扣动的地方，正是机械出了毛病

root: 希腊 mekhane「装置、手段」→ mekhanikos「装置的」→ 拉丁 mechanicus → 英语 mechanical；力学义随牛顿力学固定，比喻义「不假思索」起于近代工业与官僚重复。

sensesIntro.en: Ten senses move from machines to their working parts, the science of mechanics, unthinking habit, routine, breakdown, force ratios, machine copies, the feel of a switch and instrument drawing.
sensesIntro.cn: 十个义项从机器出发，经过工作部件、力学、不假思索、例行重复、损坏、力比、机器复制、开关手感，最后到仪器制图。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a row of meshing gears, one tooth missing, still turning and clicking in place.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排咬合的齿轮，其中一枚缺了齿，仍在原处转动并咔嗒作响。

branches.en: MACHINE AND PARTS: things of that kind, and specifically the moving layer inside a system.
branches.cn: 机器与部件：同类事物，以及系统中运动的那一层。

branches.en: SCIENCE OF FORCE: mechanics as a subject, and the measured gain a tool gives.
branches.cn: 力的科学：作为学科的力学，以及工具提供的可测增益。

branches.en: AUTOMATISM: acting without attention, and repeating without variation.
branches.cn: 自动性：不留神地行动，以及毫无变化地重复。

branches.en: HARDWARE IN THE WORLD: physical breakdown, and the feel of a real moving switch.
branches.cn: 现实中的硬件：实体损坏，以及真实运动开关的手感。

branches.en: MADE BY INSTRUMENT: copies produced by a machine, and drawings produced by a ruler.
branches.cn: 由器械造成：机器生产的复制品，以及用尺规画出的图纸。

intro.en: Mechanical is a Greek adjective ending on a Greek noun; English later added -ly for the adverb and -s for the science noun.
intro.cn: mechanical 是希腊名词加希腊形容词词尾；英语后来又加 -ly 成副词、加 -s 成学科名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin mechanicus is the borrowing that carried the Greek adjective into European languages; the ending -ical reached English through French forms.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 mechanicus 是把希腊形容词带入欧洲语言的借词；词尾 -ical 经法语形式进入英语。

items.example: The noun is the source of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是整个词族的源头。

items.example: The adjective supplies the ending that English kept.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词提供英语所保留的词尾。

items.example: The ending marks an adjective of relation.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾标记关系形容词。

items.example: The ending turns the adjective's field into a science.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把形容词所指领域变成一门学问。

items.example: The ending builds the word for an assembly of parts.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾构成「部件组合」的名称。

items.example: The adverb describes the manner of action.
items.exampleCN: 副词描述动作的方式。

items.example: Latin used the adjective as a name for a worker.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语把这个形容词用作工人的名称。

items.example: The Latin word for hand is the base of the direct opposite.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语「手」是它的直接对立词的词基。

core_image: 一排咬合的齿轮：每一枚只做一件事，连起来却推动整台机器

sceneCN: 这里 mechanism 是「机械结构、传动装置」（第 2 个义项：机器内部一起工作的部件与结构）；句意：钟表匠揭开后板，展示这座老塔钟的机械结构。场景要点：塔钟的黄铜后板、层层咬合的齿轮、钟表匠手里的放大镜；对应第 1 个义项。
